subject: Abundance data with three temporal scales. Aggregate, separate or BUGS?

messages.author: a7999634d98380ca
messages.subject: Abundance data with three temporal scales. Aggregate, separate or BUGS?
parts:
Dear list


I am relatively new to N-mixture models, but I have used dynamic occupancy modelling in the past.

Recently I have been working through the AHM book, which is absolutely the best stats book I have ever read.


I have lizard abundance data from 30 sites and 15 species, spanning three temporal scales (year/month/day). Sites vary categorically (grazed/ungrazed, road/no road, reserve/not, etc).

In the spring/summer of both 1999 and 2016, sites were surveyed for five days each in Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan (four 5-day surveys in each year; see attached).

I am interested in comparing abundance between 1999 and 2016, not between months in each year. I am also interested in interactions between year and site type, e.g. have species declined in some sites but not others.


Ideally I would build a single model for each species that accounts for daily variation in detectability (min and max temperatures) and compares years and site types, but I don't know if this is possible.

I wondered if anyone can provide any advice on the best approach to use?


Possible approaches:

1) One approach would be to aggregate detection covariates for the survey days in each month (e.g. mean maximum temperature; number of days >30'c) and use pcount with years 'stacked' and year as a fixed factor (so months are the sampling periods). I have run some trial models like this and the results seem okay. However, aggregating weather data across days within a month undoubtedly results in loss of information.


2) Is it appropriate to use pcountOpen or gpcount with year as primary period and month as secondary? again with detection covariates aggregated for each month. I only have two years and they are 17 years apart.


3) Another option would be to use gpcount to model the two years separately and later compare the parameter estimates, with month as the primary and day as the secondary periods (4 months x 5 days each). This is perhaps not very elegant, but it allows the influence of daily temperature on p to be modelled explicitly.


4) Is it possible to build a BUGS model with three temporal scales? I have no experience working with BUGS/jags except for parts of the AHM book.


Any advice you have is greatly appreciated.


Tim

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Abundance data with three temporal scales. Aggregate, separate or BUGS?
parts:
Dear Tim,
 Thanks for your kind comments on the AHM book, we appreciate it!

 I would encourage you to play around with the pcountOpen or gpcount functions and see if these models prove effective for your data. The data structure seems right for them.    The other thing to think about is to "stack" the data... take each year and treat them as a sample of new sites so that you're just modeling the within-year variation. There is a lot of discussion of this on the unmarked list.

 In Vol. 2 of AHM we intend to cover these models in some detail... Vol 2 is languishing badly I'm afraid but we'll get it done eventually, just not enough to help you right now.

regards
andy
